---
title: "View Lineage and Selected Networks"
subtitle: "How does one compiled Plan yield an ordered Direct or HB observation boundary?"
toc-depth: 2
---

**Status:** `CONVERGING` dev5 candidate implementation. The public view, PTC, and
terminal-capability contracts in
[V1 Runtime Contract](../v1-runtime-contract.qmd#shared-topology-and-unified-node-views)
remain authoritative. This page fixes the immutable lineage and selected-network
implementation evidence.

## Keep one canonical lineage grammar

Every `NetworkViewRef` starts at the sealed Plan's `original` node basis and
has exactly this shape:

```text
original
-> optional ptc(ports)
-> zero or more transform_pair(node_a, node_b, id)
-> optional terminal retain(coordinates)
```

`ptc()` is present at most once and must precede every transform and `retain()`.
Its Port arguments are validated against the same Plan, must be unique,
nonloading, and have one proved attachment/load/lowering; their semantic set is
canonicalized in Plan Port declaration order. A later call cannot add or remove PTC from a parent
Ref. Transform steps remain in declaration order because each changes the
current coordinate basis. `retain()` is terminal and preserves the caller's
declared coordinate order; empty, duplicate, foreign, stale, or unavailable
coordinates fail before execution.

Logical Port IDs, Public node IDs, and final wave-channel IDs are distinct
namespaces. A final channel is exactly its retained coordinate ID—not an alias
for a Port ID. Without `retain()`, solving uses logical Ports in Plan declaration
order. With `retain()`, final coordinate order is the public N-port order.

## Bind parameters before deriving a view

The compiler first binds the operation's complete `ParameterSet` and forms the
original physical graph. `transform_pair()` then recalculates its automatic
weights from that bound graph, for every candidate during optimization. It does
not cache baseline weights, use a previously reduced matrix, or expose manual
weights.

For a selected pair, its external capacitance cuts include ground/reference and
all nodes outside the pair; their direct mutual capacitance is excluded from
the weights but stays in the physical energy. This is the full-external-cut rule
from [Admittance Coordinate Transforms](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/network-modeling/admittance-coordinate-transforms.qmd#full-external-cut-weighting).
Each transform records its input IDs, generated `id.common` and
`id.differential` IDs, resolved real coordinate map, and evidence for
invertibility. It does not claim to diagonalize a distributed, reduced,
frequency-dependent, or nonlinear operating-point model.

## Apply topology and boundary steps in one order

PTC changes only the effective analysis load mask. It removes the matched load
of each explicitly selected nonloading probe after source-resistor
de-embedding; all other physical/environmental loads remain. The mask is
defined in original logical-Port order and is retained as evidence before and
after coordinate mapping. A transformed pair must have one common load state:
both source Port loads are compensated or neither is. Mixed state fails
preflight rather than assigning a fractional generated-channel load.

After PTC and transforms, `retain()` partitions the current basis into ordered
selected coordinates and its complement. The complement receives zero external
current and is eliminated with a factorization/linear solve—never an explicit
inverse and never a submatrix of a native S result. The boundary meaning is
maintained in [Schur Complement and Kron Reduction](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/numerical-methods/schur-complement-kron-reduction.qmd#zero-current-schur-versus-matched-wave-submatrices).

That node-coordinate partition is sufficient for Direct quantity evaluation.
It does not imply a wave boundary. If the retained terminal basis is not
Port-realizable, all eight wave-only retain records (`A`, `B`, `R`, `D`, `Q`,
the selected/omitted projectors, and omitted matched loads) use the canonical
`0 x 0` not-applicable evidence digest. The source-boundary and de-embedding
hashes bind corresponding closed not-applicable envelopes. These records must
not be read as zero physical matrices; the selected-network construction is
absent. Existing logical-Port loads remain in the complete node operator used
by the quantity procedure.

For a Port-realizable final basis, the compiler derives and records the ordered
original-Port selector $B_p$, final coordinate map $A_k$, final injection map
$B_k$, transformed reference matrix $R_k$, its principal real-SPD square root
$D_k$, and the selected/omitted projectors. In particular,

$$
B_k=B_pA_k^T,\qquad R_k=A_kR_pA_k^T,\qquad D_k=R_k^{1/2}.
$$

The root is the principal SPD root; SCNSim never substitutes diagonal entries
for a nondiagonal $R_k$. The lineage binds the exact maps, load mask, selected
and omitted partitions, and ordered coordinate IDs. Required factorization and
solve residual checks are execution-time Gates; their raw diagnostic values
are not durable Result or receipt fields. The resulting S convention is the canonical generalized power-wave
construction in
[Port Reference Impedance Semantics](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/simulation/port-reference-impedance-semantics.qmd#real-spd-matrix-reference-power-waves).

## Publish only a realizable selected network

Direct `evaluate()` and Direct optimization may use a named unported Public or
composite-exposed coordinate because they do not promise a wave network. Direct
or HB `solve()` must instead prove every final coordinate is Port-realizable:
one uniquely Port-bound original node, or a generated coordinate from an
invertible transform of a complete Port-bound subspace. Anonymous Internal
nodes are never selectable. An unported final coordinate fails rather than
receiving a special matrix-only response.

The failure is a preflight capability result: no Julia solver is launched and
no request attempt is allocated. Conversely, the quantity path consumes only
the retained/complement node lineage and never interprets the not-applicable
wave evidence as a Port selector or reference impedance.

For a valid final basis, Direct and HB both publish the same ordered N-port
selected-network families $Y^{\mathrm{view}}$, $Z^{\mathrm{view}}$, and
$S^{\mathrm{view}}$. HB first solves the full original nonlinear/static problem,
then normalizes and lowers the same PTC mask and coordinate maps at every
retained sideband replica. This leaves Direct and HB free to use their native
backends without allowing a backend-specific view or load mask.

`SParameterTrace` is a named projection of an already materialized complete
selected S matrix. Its input/output strings name final channel IDs, not logical
Port aliases; Direct uses empty mode tuples and HB uses tuples matching the
ordered pump axes. Binding a trace validates those IDs and modes but never
launches another solve or hides full S/Y/Z evidence.

## Explain without creating evidence

`run.explain(ref, spec)` validates the complete bound lineage and renders the
same deterministic preflight facts used by a terminal operation: original
Port order, node-to-Port canonicalization, PTC selection and load mask,
ParameterSet-resolved transform weights/maps, retained/complement partitions,
port-realizability, and selected-network reference construction. It performs
no Direct/HB numerical solve, creates no attempt, and writes no workspace
receipt. A failed invariant identifies its lineage step rather than producing a
smaller fallback view.
